label: Narrative experience
tagline: Immersive walk-into-this-place pieces - dramaturgy, presence, felt-state
description: Crafts pieces where the user walks into a place and leaves changed: a museum microsite that lives, an exhibition extension that breathes, a memorial that holds, a character portrait at depth, an editorial scrollytelling piece that earns its long-form. Inherits simulation-orchestrator's discipline (4 paradigms - 2d-illustrative / 3d-environment / iconographic-anim / hybrid - pipeline shape, scene-builder fanout) and the shared orchestrator-family contract: research commits a buildTier (simple / standard / full), the orchestrator scaffolds a tier-sized builder set and hands back, the caller dispatches builders in dependency order with NO per-drawer lens, the runtime/composer builder assembles runtime.html LAST, and a SINGLE final QA+lens gate judges the assembled runtime once (craft/aesthetic/concept trio; pass = QA ok AND >=2/3 lenses pass) before committing the container. What changes is purpose: where simulation gives the user UNDERSTANDING of a system, narrative-experience gives the user PRESENCE inside a place. Three structural substitutions, each in service of felt-experience: spine (the dramaturgy - authored moments, some anchored to time/scroll, some waiting in space to be found) replaces loop; reveals (the act of attention - gentle progressive discovery, plus body-carrying navigation when the scene is walkable) replaces controls; ambient (the soundscape - the room listening back) is a new first-class channel. Walkable 3D lives inside the 3d-environment paradigm; freedom of movement is the breathing room WITHIN the script, not absence of authorship. Collaborates with visual-orchestrator for raster imagery - painterly plates, character portraits, artifact close-ups, texture maps - so every asset inherits the brief's styleCue and the piece reads as one. At the final gate the concept lens scores against felt-state successFeel ('the room holds them', 'they leave quieter'), never informational outcomes, judging the four sensory channels combined on the assembled runtime. Two cross-boundary contracts the orchestrator enforces beyond that gate: §1.2 iframe ↔ host pointer + scroll contract (touch-action policy, overlay pointer-events budget, guaranteed scroll-past affordance, wheel forwarding, pointer-capture cleanup) and §5.6 Phase F layered-interaction QA + fix pass the chat caller runs - catches violations the final gate cannot see on the runtime's own surface because they live at the iframe ↔ host boundary no builder owns (canonical case: museuuum 'glitchy at entrance and i cant scroll' thread).

triggers.title: build a site with this piece
triggers.rule: User wants the experience embedded in a larger app/site (rare for narrative - most are whole-page). Top-level Claude scaffolds the shell (with nx-placeholder slot), then dispatches narrative-experience-orchestrator per slot, drives the build, embeds per the playbook.
